title: System classification
standard_note: AI SR9 corrected intent: The applicable oversight, transparency, and accountability obligations are determined by the EU AI Act risk classification assigned here. Human oversight requirements under Article 14 apply specifically to High-Risk AI systems. Portfolio-level governance monitoring applies to all tiers via Steps 12, 14, and 15.

classification_model.description: Step 3 produces a dual-axis classification record. Axis A captures the internal governance tier from the standard. Axis B captures the legal risk tier from the EU AI Act wizard. Both axes are required — they answer different questions and must coexist. The combined result determines which downstream workflow steps are mandatory.

axis_a.name: Internal governance tier
axis_a.source: AI Acceptable Use Standard — AI SR2
axis_a.purpose: Determines the intensity of internal governance process: which workflow steps are mandatory, whether AI Change Board approval is required, and the depth of due diligence.

axis_b.name: EU AI Act legal risk tier
axis_b.source: EU AI Act Classification Wizard — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
axis_b.purpose: Determines which legal obligations attach to the use case: Article obligations, harmonised standard controls, conformity assessment requirements, and the correct interpretation of AI SR9 oversight obligations.

axis_a_classification.description: Internal governance tier — complete this section first.

tiers.label: Tier 1 — General productivity
tiers.definition: Use of AI tools for general productivity purposes where the output does not directly and significantly influence business decisions, external communications, or regulated processes.

tiers.label: Tier 2 — Business-impacting content
tiers.definition: Use of AI tools to generate content that could significantly influence user decisions or actions, or that is used in regulated, external-facing, or high-stakes contexts.
examples: Translation services for external or regulated content

axis_a_classification.escalation_rule: If data identification in Step 4 reveals personal, confidential, or Group-identifying data is involved, the use case must be treated as Tier 2 regardless of content type.

axis_b_classification.description: EU AI Act legal risk tier — determined by completing Gates G1 through G5 in sequence. Gates may not be skipped except where a short-circuit outcome is explicitly defined. The wizard is authoritative for Article obligations; do not derive obligations from the tier label alone.
axis_b_classification.legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council

gates.gate_purpose: Article 5 — Identifies uses that are outright banned. Must always be completed first.
gates.short_circuit: If ANY answer is YES → classification = PROHIBITED. Assessment ends immediately. No other gates apply.

questions.question: Does the system use subliminal, manipulative, or deceptive techniques to distort a person's behaviour in a way that causes or is likely to cause harm?
Does the system exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups (age, disability, social or economic situation) to distort behaviour in a harmful way?
Does the system perform social scoring of natural persons by public authorities leading to detrimental or disproportionate treatment?
Does the system assess or predict the risk of a person committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits (not objective, verifiable facts)?
Does the system compile facial recognition databases by untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage?
Does the system infer emotions of natural persons in the workplace or educational institutions (except for safety or medical reasons)?
Does the system perform biometric categorisation of natural persons to deduce or infer race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, or sexual orientation?
Does the system use real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes (outside the narrow Article 5(2) exemptions)?

any_yes.workflow_consequence: HARD STOP — system cannot be placed on market or put into service. No compliance framework controls apply. Use case must not be built or deployed. ISG must record the prohibition determination and notify the AI Change Board.

gates.gate_purpose: Article 3(1) — Confirms the system falls within the Act's definition before applying any obligations.

questions.question: Is the system a machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment?
Are the outputs produced by the system (predictions, recommendations, decisions, content) intended to influence real or virtual environments?

any_no.workflow_consequence: EU AI Act does not apply. Internal governance tier (Axis A) still applies. Record the out-of-scope determination. No Article obligations attach.

gates.gate_purpose: Annex III + Article 6(2) — Identifies whether the use case falls within one of the eight high-risk domains.

questions.question: Does the system perform biometric identification or categorisation of natural persons?
sub_questions: Does the system identify or verify a person's identity from biometric data (face, fingerprint, iris, voice, or gait)?
Does the system categorise people based on biometric characteristics such as gender, age, or ethnicity?
Does the system match individuals against a watchlist or identity database using biometric data?
Does the system infer personal attributes or intentions from biometric signals?

questions.question: Is the system used in the management or operation of critical infrastructure (roads, water, gas, heating, electricity)?
sub_questions: Does the system manage or control road, rail, aviation, or maritime traffic?
Does the system monitor or operate water supply, gas, electricity, or heating networks?
Does the system make operational decisions affecting the safety or continuity of critical digital infrastructure?
Does the system control industrial or environmental safety equipment in critical facilities?

questions.question: Is the system used in education or vocational training — e.g. determining access, evaluating students, or monitoring during exams?
sub_questions: Does the system determine or significantly influence admissions or access to educational programmes?
Does the system assess, score, or grade students or trainees?
Does the system monitor student behaviour, attention, or activity during exams?
Does the system predict educational outcomes or determine progression pathways?

questions.question: Is the system used in employment, workers management, or self-employment — e.g. recruitment, promotion, task allocation, or performance monitoring?
sub_questions: Does the system screen, rank, or score job candidates during recruitment?
Does the system inform or make recommendations on promotion, demotion, or termination?
Does the system allocate tasks, assign workloads, or direct how work activities are carried out?
Does the system monitor or evaluate employee performance, behaviour, or location?

questions.question: Is the system used to evaluate eligibility for, or to assess, essential private or public services — e.g. credit scoring, insurance risk, emergency dispatch, social benefits?
sub_questions: Does the system assess creditworthiness or determine eligibility for loans or credit?
Does the system calculate or influence insurance premiums or risk classification?
Does the system triage, prioritise, or route emergency services requests?
Does the system determine eligibility for social benefits, housing, or public assistance?

questions.question: Is the system used by law enforcement authorities — e.g. individual risk assessment, polygraph testing, crime analytics, evidence reliability evaluation?
sub_questions: Does the system assess the likelihood of an individual committing a crime or reoffending?
Does the system detect emotional state, stress, or deception in law enforcement contexts?
Does the system evaluate the reliability of evidence, witness statements, or polygraph results?
Does the system profile individuals or groups to predict criminal activity?

questions.question: Is the system used for migration, asylum, or border control management — e.g. risk assessment of irregular migration, examination of applications, document verification?
sub_questions: Does the system assess the risk of irregular migration or the likelihood of an individual absconding?
Does the system assist in examining asylum applications or determining refugee eligibility?
Does the system verify or authenticate identity documents at border checkpoints?
Does the system profile travellers or perform risk scoring for border security purposes?

questions.question: Is the system used in the administration of justice or democratic processes — e.g. assisting courts in researching or applying law, influencing election outcomes?
sub_questions: Does the system assist courts, tribunals, or legal professionals in researching or applying law to specific cases?
Does the system assist in alternative dispute resolution such as mediation or arbitration?
Does the system influence, predict, or target electoral outcomes or voting behaviour?
Does the system generate or distribute personalised political content at scale?

any_yes.workflow_consequence: Full Chapter III Section 2 obligations apply. Conformity assessment required before deployment. AI Change Board approval is mandatory regardless of Axis A tier. Human oversight under Article 14 is a legal requirement — this satisfies the AI SR9 oversight obligation for this use case.

applicable_articles.title: Risk Management System
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: High-risk AI systems must establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system throughout the entire lifecycle.

applicable_articles.title: Data and Data Governance
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Training, validation, and testing data must meet data governance practices covering relevance, representativeness, and freedom from errors and biases.

applicable_articles.title: Technical Documentation
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Providers must draw up technical documentation before the system is placed on the market, in accordance with Annex IV.

applicable_articles.title: Record-Keeping and Logging
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: High-risk AI systems must have automatic logging capabilities to enable monitoring throughout the system's lifetime.

applicable_articles.title: Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: High-risk AI systems must provide deployers with clear instructions for use covering intended purpose, accuracy levels, risks, and human oversight measures.

applicable_articles.title: Human Oversight
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that natural persons can effectively oversee them during use, including the ability to intervene or halt the system.
applicable_articles.sr9_note: This is the legal basis for the human oversight obligation under AI SR9. It applies to this use case because it is classified High-Risk. It does not apply to Limited Risk or Minimal Risk use cases.

applicable_articles.title: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: High-risk AI systems must achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and be resilient against malicious third-party interference.

applicable_articles.title: Quality Management System
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Providers must put a quality management system in place covering policies, procedures, and systematic actions needed to achieve conformity.

applicable_articles.title: Conformity Assessment
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, providers must carry out a conformity assessment — self-assessment or third-party depending on Annex I product type.

applicable_articles.title: Post-Market Monitoring
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Providers must establish and maintain a post-market monitoring system to proactively collect and review data on performance throughout the system's lifetime.

all_no.note: System is not high-risk via Annex III. Proceed to G4 to check Article 50 transparency obligations, which may still apply.

gates.gate_purpose: Article 50 — Applies regardless of risk tier. Catches chatbots, synthetic content generators, and deepfake tools that must disclose their AI nature.
gates.note: This gate runs for ALL use cases that reach it — both High-Risk and Limited/Minimal Risk. Article 50 stacks on top of any High-Risk obligations if triggered.

questions.question: Does the system interact directly with natural persons in a conversational or text-based interface (e.g. a chatbot)?
Does the system generate synthetic audio, image, video, or text content that could deceive persons into thinking it is human-generated (e.g. deepfakes)?
Does the system generate or manipulate text that is published and could constitute information of public interest (e.g. news, public affairs content)?

any_yes.workflow_consequence: Article 50 disclosure obligations apply. The disclosure framework designed in Step 9 must specifically address these requirements. For Tier 1 use cases, this may elevate the case to Tier 2 if the disclosure obligation requires active deployment of labelling infrastructure.

applicable_articles.title: Transparency Obligations for Certain AI Systems
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: The system either interacts with humans directly, generates synthetic or deceptive content, or produces AI-generated text intended for public dissemination. Users must be informed they are interacting with AI, or that content is AI-generated, in a clear and timely manner.

gates.gate_purpose: Articles 3(4), 3(7), 25, 26 — Determines whether your organisation is a Provider (builder) or Deployer (subscriber), and identifies Article 26 obligations if applicable. Article 26 obligations only attach if the system was classified HIGH_RISK in G3.
gates.note: G5_Q0 determines organisation role for all risk levels and cascades into Step 8 risk filtering. Article 26 deployer obligations (G5_Q1) only apply if the system was classified HIGH_RISK in G3.

questions.question: How is your organisation using this AI system?

options.label: We are building or developing it
options.description: We are using APIs, open-source models, fine-tuning, or RAG to create a system tailored to our needs. We are responsible for the AI system's design and behaviour.

options.label: We are subscribing to a ready-made service
options.description: We are using a third-party AI product (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, Claude for Business, Google Workspace AI) largely as provided by the supplier.

questions.question: Is the AI system your organisation is deploying classified as high-risk and developed by a third-party provider?
Do natural persons in your organisation use the AI system's outputs to make decisions that affect other natural persons?

questions.label: Article 25 — Substantial modification check
questions.description: Answer each question about modifications you are making to the third-party AI system. Any 'Yes' may convert your Deployer role into a Provider role.
questions.soft_warning: One or more answers indicate a potential substantial modification under Article 25. This may convert your organisation's role from Deployer to Provider, triggering full Articles 9–17 obligations. Review with legal counsel before proceeding as Deployer.
questions.override_label: I have reviewed this with legal counsel — continue as Deployer

sub_questions.question: Are you fine-tuning or retraining the model on your own data?
Are you changing the system's intended purpose beyond what the provider designed it for?
Are you adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using your own proprietary datasets?
Are you integrating the system into a product where it functions as a safety-critical or regulated component?

G5_Q0_provider.note: Your organisation is acting as a Provider. Full Articles 9–17 obligations apply. OWASP implementation controls and harmonised standards controls are both relevant in Step 8.

G5_Q0_deployer.note: Your organisation is acting as a Deployer. Article 26 obligations apply if the system is high-risk. Harmonised standards controls are shown as a supplier assessment checklist in Step 8.

applicable_articles.title: Obligations of Deployers of High-Risk AI Systems
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Your organisation is a deployer of a high-risk AI system. You must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, ensure human oversight, monitor system operation, and log activity where feasible.

applicable_articles.title: Responsibilities along the AI Value Chain — Substantial Modification
applicable_articles.trigger_reason: Substantially modifying a high-risk AI system outside the provider's intended purpose makes the modifier responsible as a provider, triggering full Articles 9–17 obligations.

all_no.note: No additional deployer obligations beyond those already captured.

combined_outcome_matrix.description: Maps the intersection of Axis A and Axis B to a combined workflow consequence. The AI Change Board must be presented with both axes and the combined consequence record.

rules.label: Hard stop
rules.change_board_purpose: To formally record the prohibition determination and ensure no deployment occurs.
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: none — system must not be deployed

rules.label: Internal governance only
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Portfolio-level governance via Steps 12, 14, and 15. No per-output review requirement.

rules.label: ISG fast-track
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Portfolio-level governance via Steps 12, 14, and 15. No per-output review requirement.

rules.label: ISG fast-track with Article 50 disclosure
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Portfolio-level governance via Steps 12, 14, and 15. Article 50 disclosure controls required — consider whether disclosure infrastructure elevates this to Tier 2.
rules.escalation_note: If implementing Article 50 disclosure requires deploying labelling infrastructure or modifying external-facing systems, ISG should consider reclassifying as Tier 2.

rules.label: Full due diligence — internal governance driver
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Portfolio-level governance via Steps 12, 14, and 15. Human review checkpoints in Step 12 are internal governance controls, not Article 14 obligations.

rules.label: Full due diligence with Article 50 disclosure
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Portfolio-level governance via Steps 12, 14, and 15. Article 50 disclosure controls required and must be built into the control schedule at Step 9.

rules.label: Mandatory escalation to Tier 2 — AI Act override
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Article 14 human oversight is a legal requirement. Must be designed into the system. Satisfies AI SR9 oversight obligation for this use case.
rules.escalation_note: A Tier 1 designation is overridden when AI Act classification returns HIGH_RISK. The use case must be reclassified as Tier 2 and follow the full due diligence path.

rules.label: Full due diligence plus conformity assessment
rules.sr9_oversight_mechanism: Article 14 human oversight is a legal requirement. Must be designed into the system. Satisfies AI SR9 oversight obligation for this use case.

output_record_template.description: The completed classification record produced at the end of Step 3. This record is carried forward into all subsequent steps and included in the AI Change Board submission pack.

fields.use_case_id: string — assigned by ISG on receipt of request form
fields.classified_by: string — name and role of ISG reviewer

axis_a.escalation_applied: boolean — true if data identification forced upgrade to Tier 2

axis_b.gates_completed: string[] — e.g. [G1, G2, G3, G4, G5]
axis_b.short_circuit_gate: string | null — gate ID where assessment ended early, if applicable
axis_b.applicable_articles: article[] — full article objects from gate outcomes, accumulated across all gates
axis_b.art25_override: boolean — true if user acknowledged substantial modification warning and elected to continue as Deployer

combined_outcome.sr9_oversight_mechanism: string — the specific oversight mechanism that satisfies AI SR9 for this use case

fields.all_requirement_control_numbers: string[] — deduplicated union of all requirement_control_numbers from applicable_articles across all gates. Reserved for harmonised standards resolution in a future step.

deliverables: Completed dual-axis classification record: internal tier (Axis A) and EU AI Act outcome (Axis B)
Gate-by-gate answers for G1–G5 with question IDs recorded for audit trail
Accumulated applicable_articles list with requirement_control_numbers preserved
Combined outcome record identifying which downstream steps are mandatory
SR9 oversight mechanism statement specific to this use case
requirement_labels: AI SR9 — EU AI Act compliance (corrected: oversight obligations are tier-specific)
